text: This report responds to directions from City Council to report to the Executive Committee in 2018 with a comprehensive inventory of all capital costs associated with the spring flooding of 2017, and for the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to submit outstanding short-term capital repair and mitigation projects and longer term capital projects, arising from high lake levels, for priority consideration in the 2019 Capital Budget process. In addition, this report also outlines the cost of subsequent damage to the shoreline as a result of the windstorm experienced on April 14 and 15, 2018. The combined total cost of repairing damage across the waterfront due to these two extreme weather events is $28.267 million. A total of $24.706 million is unfunded and cannot be accommodated within the debt targets assigned to Parks, Forestry and Recreation for the 2019-2028 Capital Budget…
The Executive Committee received the report (July 6, 2018) from the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation for information.
